newsitem.title: UK: Amstrad chief sees Dancall in profits.
newsitem.headline: Amstrad chief sees Dancall in profits.

text.p: Dancall, the Danish mobile phone unit of UK consumer electronics group Amstrad Plc is seen getting back into the black in the current financial year, group chairman Alan Sugar said on Tuesday.
Sugar also denied that the Danish unit was up for sale saying Dancall would for the time being remain a 100 percent subsidiary of Amstrad.
Dancall, manufacturer of mobile telephones, reported a loss of around six million stg in 1995/96 and has recently aroused speculation about a possible takeover by one of two rival Japanese bidders.
"We did have a few false starts in the last two years...but Dancall is still a 100 percent subsidiary of Amstrad," Sugar told a news conference while launching a new Dancall mobile telephone.
Sugar said speculation had been sparked by a visit from officials of a Japanese firm who were over to discuss a contract.
In a linked move, Sugar said Dancall is due to sign manufacturing contracts with at least three global mobile phone service firms in the next few days.
"The contracts will underpin our existing capacity...so that we do not have to worry about future orders," Sugar said.
He gave no further details of the contracts.
Dancall is planning to hike its plant capacity to 90,000 units per month from a current 50,000, in the next nine to 12 months at a cost of around $10 million.
Sugar said he was confident his Dancall would continue to remain in profits after June 1997.
